newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar surges as Bonn-Buba row scares market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar surges as Bonn-Buba row scares market.

text.p: The dollar surged on Thursday as a row between Germany and its central bank deepened single currency anxiety and frightened investors into safe-haven currencies.

In equities, Paris stocks recovered strongly as investors went bargain-hunting after big losses this week triggered by fears that the left may be well placed in Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections. Elsewhere, London put on a shaky performance.

Most of the excitement was in currency markets where the dollar climbed nearly two pfennigs to 1.7067 marks, boosted by its reputation as a shelter in uncertain times after Germany's central bank denounced government plans to revalue its assets.
"If you are talking about safe-haven currencies, then sterling an the dollar spring to mind," said Stuart Frost, analyst at NatWest Markets.
By midday, however, the U.S. currency had eased back slightly and stood at 1.7028, as against 1.6905 in late Europe on Wednesday.

The Bundesbank's harsh attack on the government, which aimed to revalue gold and currency reserves to give a much-needed cash injection to public finances, sent jitters through the market in the run-up to European Monetary Union.
"This has made broad EMU more likely, but it has also made no EMU more likely than before," said Francis Breedon, senior foreign exchange economist at Lehman Brothers.
The public rift in Germany has added spice to EMU uncertainty in Europe as it follows an unexpectedly strong showing for the French Socialists party in weekend elections.

Market expectations are that if the Socialists are elected during the final run-off this weekend, they will push for Italy and Spain to be included among EMU's founding members -- watering down the euro from the start.

"The dollar should be favoured against the deutschmark because of the French elections and because the gold-revaluation rift has given a blow to Germany's reputation," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch.
The gold plan, which would help Germany reduce its deficits to make the grade for EMU, will make it difficult for Germany to reject countries such as Spain and Italy in the first round.
"The commitment to EMU from the politicians is still so immense, that I think it will be launched on time," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
Against the yen, the dollar got a boost from an unexpected fall in Japan's April industrial production, which dampened expectations of higher Japanese rates.
In equity markets, Paris soared by over one percent after closing down 3.63 percent. Wednesday's was the second big drop of the week on the enhanced prospects for the left in elections on Sunday.
Dealers said the boost came from bottom-fishing after the week's sharp falls. "This is a market of excesses," one trader said. "There have been sharp changes that didn't mean very much."
But dealers said that despite Thursday's rebound, many investors were remaining cautious because of the market's instability in recent sessions.
In London, stocks recovered after making a negative start, hit by the new uncertainty over EMU and overnight losses on the Wall Street. They were just in the plus column at lunchtime.
"The market is around its highs and when you get wobbles like these around Europe, the market's not too happy," said BZW strategist, Steve Wright.
Sterling strengthened against the mark, a factor which has squeezed profits warnings out of UK industry recently and driven share prices down.
"Sterling is back up at 2.79 (against the mark) and that's not going to help," said a dealer.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was closed because of a public holiday. Dealings on the electronic IBIS index made small gains, encouraged by the stronger dollar and shrugging off the Bonn-Buba clash.
"The market is holding on rather well," said Birgit Bachmann at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "I think the market has reacted so far relatively positively to the fight."
She said the Bundesbank showed "it was not willing to give up its historic stance and accept a weaker currency."
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7028 marks and 116.40 yen compared with 1.6902 marks and 115.86 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.5 points at 4,680.0
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 20.70 points at 2,603.87.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was closed for the day. The IBIS index was up 8.60 points at 3635.20.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $345.70 an ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $345.05 in London. Silver was two cents stronger at $4.74.
